content.title: Sentence-Ending Punctuation with Direct Quotations
content.overview: This lesson focuses on the correct placement of terminal punctuation (periods, question marks, and exclamation points) when a sentence ends with a direct quotation. It emphasizes the 'Quote-Internal Rule' and the prohibition against doubling terminal marks.
learning_objectives: Determine if quoted material functions as a question, exclamation, or statement.
Apply the Quote-Internal Rule to place punctuation correctly relative to quotation marks.
Identify and eliminate double punctuation at the end of sentences.
Select the appropriate terminal mark based on the context of the quoted words.

sections.title: The Quote-Internal Rule
sections.content: In American English, when a sentence ends with a direct quotation, the terminal punctuation typically belongs inside the closing quotation mark. If the quoted words themselves form a question or an exclamation, the question mark (?) or exclamation point (!) must be placed inside the quotation marks. If the quoted words are a simple statement, the period (.) is placed inside the quotation marks. Crucially, you should never place a terminal mark both inside and outside the quotation marks.

sections.title: Identifying Quoted Questions and Exclamations
sections.content: To decide which mark to use, isolate the words within the quotation marks. If those specific words ask a question (e.g., 'Where are you going?'), use a question mark. If they express strong emotion or a command (e.g., 'Stop right there!'), use an exclamation point. If the quoted material is just a fragment or a statement that completes the main sentence, use a period.

sections.title: Avoiding Double Punctuation
sections.content: A common error on the ACT is 'doubling up' on terminal marks. If a quotation ends with a question mark or exclamation point, the sentence is considered complete. You must not add a period after the closing quotation mark. One terminal mark is sufficient to end the entire thought.

worked_examples.question: Choose the best way to punctuate the end of the sentence: The coach looked at the scoreboard and yelled, "Run faster"
worked_examples.solution: 1. Identify the quoted words: 'Run faster'. 2. Determine the tone: The verb 'yelled' and the nature of the command indicate an exclamation. 3. Apply the rule: Place the exclamation point inside the closing quotation mark. 4. Check for doubling: Ensure no period follows the quote. Correct version: The coach looked at the scoreboard and yelled, "Run faster!"

worked_examples.question: Choose the best way to punctuate the end of the sentence: Sarah turned to her brother and asked, "Did you finish the chores."
worked_examples.solution: 1. Identify the quoted words: 'Did you finish the chores'. 2. Determine the type: This is a direct question. 3. Apply the rule: Replace the period with a question mark inside the quotation marks. 4. Final check: The sentence should end with ...chores?" with no extra period. Correct version: Sarah turned to her brother and asked, "Did you finish the chores?"

common_mistakes: Placing the question mark outside the quotation marks when the quote itself is the question.
Adding a period after a closing quotation mark that already contains a question mark or exclamation point.
Using a period for quoted words that are clearly intended to be a question based on the lead-in verb (e.g., 'asked').
exam_tips: If the lead-in verb is 'asked,' 'queried,' or 'inquired,' look for a question mark inside the quotation marks.
Read the sentence aloud; if your voice naturally rises at the end of the quote, it likely needs a question mark.
Always eliminate answer choices that feature two terminal marks (like ?." or !.") at the end of a sentence.
content.recap: When ending a sentence with a quote, place the terminal punctuation inside the quotation marks. Match the mark to the meaning of the quoted words (question, exclamation, or statement) and never use two terminal marks in a row.

knowledge_claims.content: Terminal punctuation for a direct quotation at the end of a sentence is placed inside the closing quotation mark.
Quoted words that ask a question require a question mark inside the quotation marks.
Quoted words that express strong emotion or a command require an exclamation point inside the quotation marks.
It is incorrect to place a period outside the closing quotation mark if a question mark or exclamation point is already inside.
To determine the correct punctuation, isolate the quoted words and decide if they function as a question, exclamation, or statement.
A sentence should never end with two terminal marks in a row, such as a question mark followed by a period.
The presence of the verb 'asked' before a quotation is a strong indicator that the quoted material should end with a question mark.
The 'Quote-Internal Rule' refers to the standard practice of placing periods and commas inside quotation marks in American English.
Reading a sentence aloud helps verify if the terminal punctuation matches the intended tone and structure of the quoted words.
If a quotation is a statement, a period should be placed inside the closing quotation mark to end the sentence.
Unlike some international styles, standard ACT English requires periods to be inside the closing quotation marks for terminal sentence quotes.
A question mark belongs inside the quotes only if the quoted material itself is a question, rather than the entire sentence being a question about a statement.

items.stem:
Practice form 1. Rina is editing a short report about a community garden.

Which choice is punctuated correctly?
A) Maya asked, “When will the next trial begin?”
B) Maya asked, “When will the next trial begin”.
C) Maya asked “When will the next trial begin”?
D) An unrelated condition is used instead of the stated one.

options.A: Maya asked, “When will the next trial begin?”
options.B: Maya asked, “When will the next trial begin”.
options.C: Maya asked “When will the next trial begin”?
options.D: An unrelated condition is used instead of the stated one.

items.explanation: The correct choice directly applies the target skill: 句末标点与直接引语标点.

videoLesson.description: Recognize whether quoted words are a question, exclamation, or neither based on their wording. Decide punctuation placement using the quote internal rule and avoid doubling terminal marks.
